an indeclinable noun (τὸ χρεών, τοῦ χρεών, τῷ χρεών), rare in the most ancient poetry, foreign to Homer, about which I have spoken in the Thesaurus, vol. 8 p. 1640. Similar to the Ionic feminine ἡ χρεώ, which Homer already used. The Attics, however, often used it either with the article τὸ χρεών or without the article in place of χρή (it is necessary), especially by the tragic poets, where the meter required a disyllabic form: of which kind very many examples are found in the sixth foot of trimeters.
τὸ χρεών that which is necessary.
to suffer what is not fated.
it is necessary that he be one of your descendants.
Thus it is necessary to insult those who insult.
